R3-01.why: The theme ('mess up the house, hide it before Mom gets home') is instantly relatable and the PARTY phase is self-explanatory, but a round runs through 4 phases with 3 different control schemes (free roam, then an elevated tap-to-hide view, then hunt). The Parent switches from a lane-dodge driving game to a gadget radial, and hidden rules (FREEZE threshold, Decoy, Snitch, gossip postcards) need explaining. A kid who joins mid-round, or gets picked as Parent first, will be lost.
R3-01.fix: Cut to 3 phases: make the drive a non-interactive 10-second cutscene, or give the Parent a simple pre-hunt peek. Lock Snitch and Decoy behind the second match, and never make a player's first match a Parent match; seat them as a Kid with a pictogram-only phase banner.

R3-02.why: 'Draw a shape, a spell fires' passes the 5-second test, and there is no thumbstick or camera to manage. But kids must memorize 6 runes, hit a 1-second fusion timing window, learn which fusion beats which enemy, and read relic text between waves. Messy finger traces on small phones will misfire often, which reads as 'I did it wrong' more than comedy for 8-year-olds.
R3-02.fix: Keep rune guides on screen permanently as a small corner legend. Make the suggested partner rune flash on the enemy itself, so 'draw what the monster shows' replaces memorizing counters. Replace relic text with icon-plus-preview animations and widen the fusion window to about 2 seconds for new players.

R3-03.why: Red Light Green Light is already known to almost every child, and 'let go of the stick = freeze' with an auto-pose and a 'LIGHT COMING' warning teaches itself in seconds. Points come off because the Mischief objective is fuzzy (only some pranks are live, some are hidden and must be found), and the Guard role (aiming the beam, ignoring decoy NPC statue movement, managing battery) is hard for younger kids, so losing as the Guard can feel unfair.
R3-03.fix: Mark every live prank with a big floating icon and a progress pip on the Mischief meter, and drop hidden pranks for new players. Give rookie Guards a more generous lock-on and battery, and make Guard opt-in until a player has played 3 rounds as a statue.

R3-04.why: The input is about as simple as it gets: one big HOLD button, no thumbstick, auto camera, a tandem tutorial and a 'paddle now' ghost arrow. The goal (get down the river, don't sink) is obvious. The hard part is understanding that your one paddle only turns part of a shared raft, and coordinating 6 strangers without chat. Per-vehicle seat roles and Versus water-bailing add rules on top, so early runs may feel random or frustrating, and the blame card can sting young kids.
R3-04.fix: Show each player's paddle side with a big colored arc and give instant per-seat feedback ('your paddle turned us LEFT'). Keep role seats (Lookout, Bailer) locked until players have finished a few runs, and frame the blame card as playful (silly tags, no single 'culprit' callout) for under-13s.

R3-05.why: 'Spray the fire, save the puppy' is the clearest objective of the set and has strong emotional pull for 8–12s; magnetized hose sweeping is forgiving and pulsing critter icons tell kids where to go. The cost is control and rule load: thumbstick plus right-half drag plus a context button (with jump nearby) is a two-thumb setup, and grease/foam, breaker, water-refill, run-and-the-critter-escapes and drag-the-downed-teammate rules each need teaching.
R3-05.fix: Have the hose auto-aim at the nearest fire when held (keep drag for advanced players) and move the hose drag zone away from the jump button. Introduce one special rule per alarm level with a visible cause and effect (grease flares in orange, foam glows next to it), so alarm level 1 is pure spray-and-save.

overall_notes: No concept is clearly top-quartile on child accessibility. The best are the ones that build on mental models kids already have (Red Light Green Light in R3-03, firefighter-rescues-pet in R3-05) or that minimize input (R3-04). The common weakness is layered rules that are hidden or need reading: Snitch/Decoy/gadgets (R3-01), fusion pairings and relic text (R3-02), hidden pranks (R3-03), seat roles (R3-04), fire types (R3-05). Asymmetric 1vN games (R3-01, R3-03) also carry the risk of a child being handed the harder solo role on their first match. Gating secondary rules behind early play-count would lift every concept by about 1 point.
